title: cohorted-priming-procedure-and-stability-checklist
content:
Summary:

This is a working note describing a new harness methodology intended to improve repeatability and reduce stochastic variance in throughput benchmarking for the serving runtime. The core idea: group virtual clients into stable cohorts with deterministic priming checkpoints + occupancy-aware monitoring so we can (1) isolate systemic bottlenecks, (2) produce repeatable throughput curves across runs, and (3) make warmup/priming cost explicit rather than implicit.

Motivation / observed problems we want to address:
- High run-to-run throughput variance (5–15%) despite identical config; noise concentrated in the first 2–5 minutes.
- Warmup heuristics (fixed-duration priming) mask occupancy effects: same-duration priming yields different steady-state occupancy for different sequence-length mixes.
- Client RNG and prompt-bank selection create subtle cache/KV divergence between runs.
- Long tails due to transient batching mismatch when bursty clients sync up.

Goals:
- Produce a repeatable throughput benchmark with <3% run-to-run median throughput variance for common customer profiles.
- Provide an actionable checklist to detect when variance is due to workload vs infra.
- Explicitly measure warmup cost (tokens & time) and report steady-state onset time.

Definitions / metrics to record (mandatory):
- offered_qps: requests per second attempted by loadgen (per-cohort and aggregate).
- achieved_throughput_tokens_per_sec: actual served tokens/s measured at runtime (token accounting hooks in runtime).
- p50/p95/p99 latency (server and end-to-end).
- batch_occupancy_histogram: distribution of batch sizes observed by the inference runtime.
- kv_hit_rate and prefix_cache_hit_rate (if enabled).
- priming_token_count and priming_wall_time per cohort.
- client_sync_index: simple counter to detect synchronized bursts across cohorts.

Key new ideas in this methodology:
1) Cohorted clients with fixed seed banks:
   - Partition virtual clients into small cohorts (default 8–16 clients/cohort).
   - Each cohort has its own prompt-bank shard and RNG seed namespace. The seed namespace is stable across runs (seed id + cohort id).
   - This ensures that the same client cohort exercises a similar sequence-length/temperature mix across runs, reducing cross-run cache divergence.

2) Checkpointed priming sequences (deterministic priming checkpoints):
   - Instead of a timer-based warmup, run a deterministic set of priming traces per cohort that write predictable KV/prefix cache patterns (e.g., 100 prompts that exercise typical long and short sequences).
   - After priming, checkpoint a minimal priming-trace hash (sha256 of prompts and seed) and attach to run metadata. This helps detect accidental prompt-bank drift.

3) Multi-stage warmup with occupancy targets:
   - Stage A (fast probe): low-rate pass to discover model/kernel slow-paths (10% target occupancy). 2–3 minutes.
   - Stage B (occupancy ramp): steadily increase offered_qps for each cohort until observed batch_occupancy reaches the target occupancy band for the workload (configurable; e.g., 60–80% of max batch size).
   - Stage C (stabilize): hold at target for N samples (default 120s) and confirm steady-state via throughput and occupancy stability checks.

4) Occupancy-aware admission + jittered interleaving:
   - Loadgen must include slight deterministic jitter per-cohort to avoid synchronized request alignment (microbursts). Jitter window derived from cohort id and run-seed.
   - When batch occupancy drifts outside tolerance, trigger a gentle admission backoff on that cohort rather than global stop/start.

5) Checkpointed trace replay for regression debugging:
   - Capture a compressed trace (prompt ids, seeds, timing deltas) for short windows with abnormal occupancy/latency patterns. Store with run metadata to allow deterministic replay locally.

Sample loadgen config (conceptual flags) that implements the method:
- --cohorts=12
- --cohort-prompt-shards=12
- --seed-namespace=run-20241002-aisha-v1
- --priming-checkpoint=primeset-v3
- --warmup-stages=probe:120,ramp:900,stabilize:120
- --occupancy-target=0.72
- --deterministic-jitter-ms=5
- --trace-sampling=on:0.01 (1% of requests)

Practical checklist before a run (to improve reproducibility):
- [ ] Confirm prompt-bank checksum matches run metadata (priming checkpoint).
- [ ] Ensure model binary and kernel versions pinned and recorded.
- [ ] Clear or snapshot prefix/KV cache if trying to measure cold-starts.
- [ ] Confirm node GPU utilization < 5% at experiment start (avoid background jobs).
- [ ] Confirm autoscaler disabled or pinned to fixed capacity for the run.
- [ ] Start run with log-level=info and metrics sampling=1s.

Run validation and pass/fail criteria (automated):
- After Stage C stabilize, compute sliding-window throughput variance (30s windows over 120s): if stdev/mean > 0.03, mark run flaky and archive traces for investigation.
- If batch_occupancy variations exceed +/-10% of target band, fail and annotate which cohorts drifted.
- If kv_hit_rate deviates >5% vs reference run, flag as data divergence.

Debugging heuristics when runs diverge:
- If divergence occurs immediately after priming: verify priming checkpoint hash; check for prompt-bank drift or seed namespace mismatch.
- If divergence appears after occupancy ramp: inspect batch_occupancy_histogram and client_sync_index for synchronized bursts.
- If divergence is steady but higher latency: check for kernel selection differences (kernel version tags in runtime logs).
- If divergence manifests as intermittent spikes: enable higher trace sampling and collect a 30s deterministic trace for replay.

Reporting artifact for each run (automatically produced):
- run_manifest.json (metadata: seed namespace, priming hash, model binary tag, node list)
- metrics.csv (1s granularity of the mandatory metrics list)
- occupancy_profile.png (visualization)
- trace_archive.tar.gz (sampled deterministic traces)
- run_conclusion.txt (pass/fail summary + quick notes)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Evaluate how many cohorts is optimal for small vs large machines. Suggested: run sensitivity sweep [4,8,12,24].
- Explore automated priming sequence gen that maximizes KV surface coverage with minimal tokens. Can we use coverage-guided selection? (Experiment idea).
- Integrate priming checksums into model rollout CI so training or tokenizer changes break bench reproducibility early.
- Define standard reference workload profiles (e.g., chat-short, chat-long, search-rerank) and build canonical priming sets for each.

Immediate next experiments to run (short-term):
1) Baseline sweep: run existing timer-based warmup vs checkpointed-priming on same cluster and compare throughput variance across 20 runs. (Owner: Marco)
2) Cohort-count sensitivity: test cohorts=[4,8,16,32] with identical client load and record occupancy variance. (Owner: Sofia)
3) Trace-replay fidelity: produce deterministic 60s replay from archived trace and validate identical batch occupancy and throughput on a staging node. (Owner: Ethan)

Notes to self / team: this is intentionally conservative and operational—goal is to reduce “it failed once” flakiness that blocks PR benchmarks. Keep priming sets small and well-documented. When in doubt, collect more deterministic metadata (seed, checksum) than you think you need.

Links and references:
- Bench repo PR (implementation of cohorted seed namespaces): https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/412
- Current jittered-loadgen implementation (internal): RFC-PRIMING-27
- Example flaky run (archived traces): JIRA-INF-983

End of note.
